title: Microtrace synthesis workflow for e2e latency curves
body:
Purpose:
This doc describes a practical workflow to synthesize short, high-fidelity microtraces from sampled production traces and synthetic inputs. The goal is to reconstruct robust end-to-end (p50/p95/p99) latency surfaces across seqlen and tenant mixes without replaying full-production traffic or storing massive full-trace archives.

Motivation and constraints:
- We need fast, repeatable experiments to evaluate: batching changes, KV cache strategies, routing fallbacks, and model-variant swaps.
- Full replays are costly (storage/ops) and brittle (sensitive to external infra).
- Many production traces are sparse (missing stage timings) or have redaction. We want a way to synthesize realistic microtraces that preserve per-stage timing distributions and joint correlations that drive tail behavior.

Key ideas (high level):
1) Stratified micro-sampling: pick short trace windows (1-20 tokens emitted) stratified by seqlen, route, and tenant QPS.
2) Stage marginal profiling: build per-stage empirical distributions conditioned on cohort (seqlen, cold/hot cache, batch size).
3) Copula stitching: reconstruct joint timing behavior across stages by sampling marginals and correlating via an empirically fit rank-copula (preserves tail coupling).
4) Jittered replay harness: synthesize requests that exercise the runtime in staging with controlled concurrency and inter-arrival jitter to reproduce microburst and queuing effects.

Workflow (step-by-step):
A. Data selection and sketching (collection)
   - Pull 3 days of sampled traces from prod meter with trace-level metadata: seqlen, model, kv-cache-hit, route-tag, node-hash. Prefer sampling weight biased toward recent regressions.
   - From each trace extract stage timing vector: [tokenize_ms, encode_ms, model_exec_ms, kv_lookup_ms, batch_wait_ms, postproc_ms, serialize_ms, egress_ms]. If a stage is missing, mark as NA.
   - Aggregate into cohort buckets: short (<=32), mid (33-256), long (>256); cache-hot/hot-warm/cold; routing: local/remote/fallback.

B. Marginal fit and summary artifacts
   - Compute empirical CDFs per-stage per-cohort. Store quantile vectors at these breakpoints: 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99, 0.999.
   - Fit light-weight parametric approximations where sensible (log-normal or gamma) and keep the goodness-of-fit (KS stat as string).
   - Produce stage covariance matrix from rank-transformed timings (Spearman). This is small (~8x8) and portable.

C. Copula-based microtrace synthesizer
   - Algorithm summary: sample uniform vectors from an N-dim Gaussian copula parametrized by the observed Spearman correlations, map each dimension through the inverse empirical CDF for the target stage/cohort.
   - Advantages: preserves marginal shapes and tail coupling. Works with missing data by conditioning on available dims and imputing with cohort medians.
   - Output: N synthetic microtraces per cohort, each being a stage timing vector plus metadata flags (cache, seqlen, route).

D. Jittered replay harness (staging)
   - Convert microtrace stage timings into synthetic request templates: specify target seqlen, model, and per-stage wallclock offsets.
   - Replay harness will: submit requests to staging runtime with controlled client-side concurrency and inter-arrival time distribution (Poisson + microbursting pattern).
   - Use node pinning to exercise specific GPU pools (A100x2, 8xA100 clusters).
   - Capture full traces in staging including queuing/batcher states and real scheduling contention.

E. Validation and surface reconstruction
   - Compare synthesized replay p50/p95/p99 to the original production snapshots on these axes: per-stage quantiles, aggregate E2E quantiles, and tail-event fingerprints (e.g., multi-stage amplification where small increases in batch_wait_ms cascade to p99 model_exec).
   - Compute KL divergence between original and synthesized E2E latency histograms; set threshold (e.g., KL < 0.15) as acceptable fidelity for experiment use.

F. Experiment matrix examples (how to use)
   - Batching experiment: baseline adaptive-batcher v1 vs v2. For each cohort, synthesize 10k microtraces, replay at QPS levels [50, 200, 800]. Look at p50/p95/p99 and per-stage breakdown changes.
   - Cache policy eval: simulate TTL reduction and cold-start fraction increases from 2% to 15% and observe p99 uplift.
   - Model variant fallback: create synthesized traces that trigger fallback routes 0/1/5% and validate graceful degradation latency surface.

Observed exemplar outputs (toy numbers from last run in staging):
   - Test harness run: 2025-11-05, cohort mid (33-256), target QPS 200, concurrency 80
   - E2E: baseline p50=42ms, p95=220ms, p99=560ms
   - After adaptive-batcher change: p50=40ms, p95=180ms, p99=420ms
   - Per-stage delta at p99 (model_exec + batch_wait + kv_lookup): +0ms -> -60ms -> -80ms respectively (indicates batch_wait reduced tail amplification and kv_lookup benefited from smaller per-batch variance).

Failure modes and caveats:
- If production sampling is biased (e.g., only traces with errors are kept), marginals will be skewed; always compare basic coverage stats.
- Copula approach preserves rank correlation but not higher-order structural dependencies that depend on request payload complexity (e.g., per-token branching in decode).
- Replayed inter-arrival patterns must match production microburst fingerprints or queuing effects will mismatch tails.
- Staging infra must be configured to mirror production admission controls (rate limiters, token buckets) or syntheses will be non-representative.

Operational checklist (quick):
[ ] export 3 days trace sketch (bucketized)
[ ] compute marginals + Spearman matrix
[ ] produce 20k microtraces per cohort
[ ] run jittered replay at target QPS/concurrency combos
[ ] collect staging traces and compute KL & per-stage p99 diffs
[ ] open PR with both artifacts and gating thresholds

Unresolved / research questions:
- What's the minimal sample size per cohort for stable p99 synthesis? (empirically seems ~5k but need more runs)
- Can we hybridize with a small number of full replays to calibrate higher-order dependencies and reduce KL further?
- How to encode payload-dependent model_exec variance (e.g., long tail due to complex LM attention patterns) into the copula without full payloads?

Notes to self / meeting fodder:
- Show Liam the Spearman matrices next sync; they expose surprising strong coupling between batch_wait and kv_lookup on cold cache flows.
- Consider adding a small CI job that runs the microtrace synthesizer weekly against mainline to detect emergent tail regressions early.

References and quick links:
- synthesis harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-synthesizer
- staging replay infra: infra/staging/replay/README.md
- visualization confluence: confluence:latency-visualizations-v2

Appendix (compact):
- Stage names used: tokenize_ms, encode_ms, model_exec_ms, kv_lookup_ms, batch_wait_ms, postproc_ms, serialize_ms, egress_ms
- Cohorts: short<=32; mid 33-256; long>256; cache: hot/hot-warm/cold; route: local/remote/fallback

End.
